title: Heat Pumps vs Gas Boiler Running Costs... The TRUTH
summary: UK installer argues heat pumps cost more than gas boilers on standard tariffs but less with heat pump tariffs, batteries, solar and optimisation apps, with customer testimonials.

assertions.quote: It's taking heat from the outside and moving it in.
you're paying 50% more per unit of heat with a heat pump under these conditions.

verdicts.note: When the electricity-to-gas price ratio exceeds the seasonal COP divided by boiler efficiency, as on UK standard tariffs with average COPs, heat pumps cost more per unit of heat.

assertions.quote: just by being on the right tariff, the economics flip entirely.

verdicts.note: Off-peak and heat pump tariffs cut the average price paid per kWh when heating can be shifted, lowering running cost.

assertions.quote: payback sometimes being as little as 2 to 4 years.

verdicts.note: Independent estimates of home battery payback from tariff arbitrage are typically closer to a decade, not a few years.

assertions.quote: some of these apps claim to save you between 20 and 40% on your heat pump running costs.

verdicts.note: The cited savings are vendor-reported and not independently measured.

RMI finds that shifting load into cheap hours saves a lot for water heating ($154 to $48 a year in Houston) but only a few dollars a year for space heating, because a house cannot be overheated or hold heat like a tank.

UK Cosy-tariff households shifted large amounts of heat pump load into cheap hours, and about 70% of surveyed customers said they do it with smart thermostats or automation; the paper says automation makes shifting easy but cannot separate its effect from other mechanisms.

assertions.quote: with a heat pump, you can generate your own electricity via solar.
a well-designed heat pump that's using one or more of these other levers should cost less to run than a boiler.

verdicts.note: US modelling finds efficient heat pumps lower bills for many gas-heated homes, but where gas is cheap relative to electricity many see higher bills.
Typical measured savings versus gas are small or negative; halving bills happens mainly when replacing oil, propane or resistance heat.

Even national average site energy savings are 31-47% depending on efficiency, and bill savings are smaller because electricity costs more per unit; average bill savings are $100 (minimum-efficiency) to $740 a year.

Edwards' Monte Carlo bill model finds only 53% of households would clearly see lower energy bills from a heat pump, 19% would pay more and 28% show no clear change, which contradicts a general halving of bills.
In RMI's gas retrofits, energy costs rise with a heat pump in Chicago and Providence and fall only modestly in Houston and Oakland.
Cost reductions were 26-40% against propane furnaces and 53-56% against electric resistance, so 'half or more' held only for resistance-heated homes.
In the UK, replacing a gas boiler with a heat pump raised measured running costs by about £190/yr on a standard tariff, far from halving bills, even though energy use fell 40%.

assertions.quote: the uncomfortable truth is that actually both can be right.
The difference is how it's designed and how it's set up.

verdicts.note: Field studies link poor sizing, charge, airflow and commissioning to substantially lower measured efficiency.
